This is basically Terraria light, with horizontal movement rather than vertical.

You dig and explore to gather resources and equipment, fight enemies, build devices that let you craft stuff, take on bosses to continue the story...

It's fun and enjoyable. There's less content than Terraria, which is normal since the game is in early access and Terraria has had many years of updates.

I'd love to see this game add puzzles, this would set it apart and would fit well with the theme of exploring the underground and encountering ruins of ancient civilizations.

If it's this good in early access - it is going to be a huge hit when it's released.

It's a lot like stardew valley with a bit of minecraft and terraria. You dig around to get materials to buy work benches to craft gear. You can have gardens to grow food and you can build little houses to attract a very small limited amount of vendors.

-When you craft upgraded gear you can track down world bosses to unlock more crafting options.
-Characters are not attached to your world which means you can move them from world to world. Huge plus here.
-There is a hunger bar that forces you to eat food. I hate this feature but some people don't mind it
-There are ways to auto mine nodes to auto produce bars for ease of crafting and expansion.
-You can create auto farm rooms to passively gain monster mats.
-You can play with your friends
-It has progression based skill levels and stat levels. You can put points in nodes to increase their output.
-It has rare gear drops which increases the value of farming bosses.

Overall It is a great game to play through at least once. Replay value isn't really there at all. Content isn't added often, needs a modding community to keep it alive. Overall for me it was a solid 8/10.

Core Keeper is essentially Terraria Zelda with Harvest Moon vibes. It's the kind of game rich with adventure, but also rich with base building, both practical and aesthetic. It also has a LOT of quality of life features I wish games like Terraria had, so even though it isn't as expansive as games like Terraria (yet) it seems to have a better foundation so far.

It's a little bare-bones currently, yet I've thoroughly enjoyed 45 hours of it already. I wouldn't be surprised if in a year from now there was at least like 60+ hours of content, which is fantastic for a $10 game.

I enjoyed the first 3-4 hours and beating the first 3 bosses however, the game quickly becomes repetitive and boring after that. 
The gameplay loop doesn't change or evolve, what I experienced in the first 3 hours was what I was doing for the rest of the game. You gather resources and mine ore to craft gear and progress through the various milestones, pretty standard survival mechanics. Some people like this grind, I personally find it boring. 

Combat is simplistic and quickly gets boring. There is no creativity in any of the weapons. The melee sword swings, ranged weapons shoots projectiles and magic weapons are basically ranged weapons with mana. The first set of weapons I crafted work exactly the same as mid to late game weapons. There are so few unique and interesting weapons. 

There is also a shocking lack of enemy variety in this game. 2-3 enemies per biome and 2-3 enemies per sub biome is not enough enemy variety. Fighting the same monsters can get pretty repetitive.

Challenging but not too complicated, the perfect mix of tight controls, fun crafting options, and none of the annoyance of needing so many hard to find items to craft necessities. I get lost in it for hours and time flies by thanks to its great soundtrack.

Core Keeper feels like Terraria's cozy cousin. Exploration is great, the world is fun to uncover, and while there's a bit of grind, it's never excessive.

Automation is fairly basic, but incredibly satisfying. There's something rewarding about turning repetitive tasks into a well-oiled system.

The bosses are surprisingly fun too. Don't expect Mythic WoW mechanics, but they require enough strategy to keep things interesting. Add a good amount of build variety and equipment choices, and you've got a game that's easy to sink dozens of hours into.

Overall, a small gem that's well worth your time.

I loved the game and would recommend it if they fixed a bug that renders the game unplayable.
As a disabled player I use a controller+mouse system since only my right hand fingers work. The controller stick has been remapped to output WASD keys. I push the stick with my left hand wrist to move around and this far this system has worked for all other games except Core keeper.
Even though the controller has been disabled in the game settings, Core Keeper still detects it and removes the mouse cursor every time I move so I can't aim with slingshot or sword and will die to mobs very easily. It also makes interacting with ingame objects difficult. I gave up playing after countless deaths months ago and this far all my feedback and bug reports have gone unnoticed.

***I will change this review once this bug has been fixed and I can finally play the game***

6/10. I give this game a lukewarm yes.

For the price, I would recommend other games such as Terraria, Valheim, and Stardew Valley as they have way more content to enjoy and a more rewarding experience. This game is in Early Access, so there are still elements to be added, but the overall core gameplay cycle (ex. explore new biome, farm resources, kill boss) is unrewarding and therefore boring. The game is very grindy, but doesn't reward the player adequately for all their hard work. Bosses will drop items that are significantly worse than items you can find on basic mobs. The boss fights themselves are ResidentSleeper. The main goal of the game is to kill the bosses and outside of that there isn't much else to do. So if you are a goal-oriented player, then I think you'll find the experience lacking and un-fun.

The positives are that the game isn't buggy ~ especially considering its Early Access state. The graphics are cute. And playing with friends is fun and makes the game playable. There's a lot of potential with interesting elements like pets, shopkeepers, and automation.

If you buy this game, I don't think you'll hate it. I don't think you'll love it either though.

In my mind, this game sits somewhere between Terraria, Minecraft, Don't Starve Together, Enter the Gungeon, and Stardew Valley. The game tries to copy some of the known gameplay loop mechanics of the games that inspired it and it does an OK job of it. That's kind of where it sits right now, it's an OK game but I've yet to see anything it does so well than the games that inspire it other than the fancy stylized pixelated design and that really cool lighting system.

There is so much potential in this game and I will hang around to see where the devs take it after it leaves EA.
